title: NASA Study: Space Station Astronauts Chronically Sleep-Deprived, Often Use Medication
summary: NASA data shows that astronauts aboard the International Space Station frequently sleep fewer than six hours per night despite eight-and-a-half-hour allocations, with three-quarters using sleep medication.
takeaways: 44% of ISS nights: sleep less than 6 hours despite 8.5 hours scheduled
ISS average: 6.09 hours/night; shuttle average: 5.96 hours/night
75% of astronauts reported using sleep medication in orbit
Zolpidem ~75% of medicated shuttle nights; extended-release added 12%
61 of 78 shuttle crew took sleep drugs on 52% of in-flight nights; 60% before spacewalks
Hypnotic use ~20x higher than general US population

title: NASA discovers evidence of repeated water activity on Mars
summary: NASA's Perseverance rover found evidence that rocks in Mars' Jezero Crater interacted with water on at least three separate occasions, including carbon-dioxide-rich groundwater activity, an ancient lake phase, and heated underground-water events. The findings preserve evidence relevant to searching
takeaways: Three separate water-interaction episodes detected in Jezero Crater
SuperCam analyzed 185+ bedrock targets for chemistry and mineralogy
First episode: CO2-rich groundwater reacting with olivine created carbonate ridges
Later event produced calcium sulfate and fluorite mineral veins from heated water
Sequence determined but timing of events remains unknown

title: NASA images new lunar impact crater from rare event
summary: NASA's Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter discovered crater McGetchin, the largest newly formed impact crater in the solar system at 728 feet wide and 141 feet deep, formed between April and May 2024. The impact, caused by a 3–6 story asteroid, represents a rare lunar event occurring roughly once per cent
takeaways: Crater McGetchin: 728 feet wide, 141 feet deep
Formed April 11–May 22, 2024
Impactor estimated 3–6 stories tall
Such large impacts occur approximately once every 132 years
Three times larger than previous record holder from a decade earlier
Material ejected over 66 miles across lunar surface
Findings published September 16, 2026 in Science Advances
